audit: 2026-09-16 scheduled remote agent (fifth fire of the day): one 50 question batch across all four modules, published as seven files data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-16_e_<module>_N.json. Split 16 Paediatrics, 16 Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 9 Psychiatry and 9 Medicine; tier mix 28 L3, 19 L4 and 3 L5 with no L1 and no L2, taking the bank to 6692 with Paediatrics and Obstetrics on 1677 and Psychiatry and Medicine on 1669. Cell selection: the live matrix before this fire showed Paediatrics and Obstetrics on 1661 and Psychiatry and Medicine on 1660, with L3 deficits against the ideal 50 per cent of 13.52 points in Paediatrics, 13.10 in Obstetrics, 12.35 in Medicine and 11.45 in Psychiatry, L4 deficits against 45 per cent of 13.03, 12.55, 11.63 and 10.48 respectively, and L5 at 5.06 to 5.12 per cent in every module, a deficit of about minus 0.06 points. The strict per question argmax remains degenerate for the twelfth consecutive fire. Run faithfully, including the routine's 0.5 point tie break clause resolved toward the lower module total, it placed all 50 questions into Paediatrics and Obstetrics and none into Psychiatry or Medicine, because the Medicine and Psychiatry L3 deficits sit 1.2 and 2.1 points behind the Paediatrics L3 leader and so never enter the near tie window at all. That allocation would have carried Paediatrics and Obstetrics to 1686 against 1660, a spread of 26, breaching the Section 2 module balance directive that all four modules stay within about 10 of each other, which the routine prompt itself cites as the authority for the tie break. This fire therefore treated the deficit ranking as governing the weighting and the module balance cap as bounding the skew, allocating 16/16/9/9 so that the resulting spread is 8 and remains inside the cap while still directing twice as much volume to the two modules carrying the largest L3 and L4 deficits. Within each module the tier split followed the ideal shape weighted toward L3, whose deficit leads L4 by 0.5 to 1.0 points everywhere. L5 was held at 3 questions, about 6 per cent of the batch, rather than the strict zero the argmax produces, because the standing long term target is to maintain L5 at 5 per cent in each module and an all L3/L4 batch decays that share every fire; post publication L5 sits at 5.07, 5.07, 5.03 and 5.15 per cent. The structural point for the maintainer is unchanged and now has twelve fires of evidence behind it: because L5 sits at target its deficit can never approach the 11 to 14 point deficits carried by L3 and L4, and because the legacy L2 block of 353 to 422 questions per module sits permanently in the denominator, those L3 and L4 deficits can never close either, so the unmodified argmax will never select an L5 cell and will always concentrate on whichever one or two modules lead on L3 deficit. The two rules need reconciling in the routine prompt itself rather than re-adjudicated each fire.
